note: Locations the atlas does not print. The Night City Atlas gives the Exec Zone no numbered locations at all and four other districts only one or two, which leaves them somewhere the player can be sent and nowhere they can stand: no tags, so no actions, no dials, no beats, and no building for a job to be at. This file is the ground those districts need, and it is a HOUSE RULE for exactly the reason travel time is — night-city.json stays what the publisher printed, and geography.ts appends these to it. A second, smaller set gives a lived-in district its ordinary evening: somewhere to drink and somewhere to eat where the atlas prints neither, because a player asking for a bar in their own neighbourhood should not be told the nearest one is across a district line. A third set, added with the shops and clinics a character can travel to, gives every district somewhere to be cut and, in the districts the atlas leaves bare, somewhere to buy: fifteen clinics, so that each home district has a ripperdoc of its own to keep (the haunt rule puts people near home), and ten shops, so that no district is without a seller and the map has more than three places that sell a gun.
sourceNote: Nothing here is invented from nothing. Every entry is built out of what the atlas does print about its district: its security provider, its gangs, its city manager, the streets the map labels, and the dossier written from the published description. Codes continue each district's own numbering.

exec_zone.name: Zone Station
exec_zone.blurb: The private monorail terminus. Corporate authorization, credentials and biometrics decide who boards, and the seating is ranked.

exec_zone.name: Executive Zone Oasis
exec_zone.blurb: An Oasis unlike any other in Night City, stocking premium brands and rarities. Fresh-cut flowers, delivered by drone.

exec_zone.name: The Davies Estate
exec_zone.blurb: Home of Doctor Karen Davies and the seat of the Home Owner's Association, which is the whole of the district's government.

exec_zone.name: The Greens
exec_zone.blurb: A private club with courses, courts, a spa and a dining room. Membership is not a thing money alone has ever bought.

exec_zone.name: Lazarus Gatehouse
exec_zone.blurb: Where the district decides whether you are coming in. Lazarus staffs it around the clock and keeps its own records.

exec_zone.name: The Verge
exec_zone.blurb: The tent community crowding the ground outside the wall, much to the irritation of the people whose views include it.

exec_zone.name: The Aurelian Suite
exec_zone.blurb: A wellness suite for residents, staffed by a surgeon on retainer to the Home Owner’s Association and, by extension, to your neighbours’ secrets. The appointment book is the most guarded document in the district.

reclamation_zone.name: The Yard
reclamation_zone.blurb: The depot the reclaimers run Night City's public transportation out of. Everything that moves people is repaired here.

reclamation_zone.name: The Swap
reclamation_zone.blurb: Where reclaimed parts change hands. Provenance is not a question anybody working the tables considers polite.

reclamation_zone.name: The Long Camp
reclamation_zone.blurb: Where the families who took this land for the work live on it. Nomad ground, settled, and not entirely settled about that.

reclamation_zone.name: Bay Nine
reclamation_zone.blurb: A bay at the back of the Yard where a reclaimer medtech fits transit-grade prosthetics: heavy, ugly and guaranteed to outlast the tram they were salvaged from.

heywood_docks.name: Cargo Way Wharf
heywood_docks.blurb: The berths the smaller Corporate-sponsored ships use, working up and down the West Coast where the big vessels cannot.

heywood_docks.name: The Weighbridge
heywood_docks.blurb: SK Security's counting house. Nothing leaves the docks without being weighed, logged, and matched against a manifest.

heywood_docks.name: Skiv's Counter
heywood_docks.blurb: A dockside bar the Skiv Family keep an office at the back of. Both halves of the business are open to anyone.

heywood_docks.name: Berth Nine
heywood_docks.blurb: A shipping container fitted out as a surgery and bolted to the end of Cargo Way. Stevedores, sailors and the Skiv Family’s people use it, and the whiteboard by the door lists who owes what.

norcal_military_base.name: The Main Gate
norcal_military_base.blurb: Where the Estero Bay Military COG decides whether NorCal has business with you. The NorCal Military Police staff it.

norcal_military_base.name: The Motor Pool
norcal_military_base.blurb: Vehicles, munitions and the people who keep both running, on land traded to Militech for training and materiel.

norcal_military_base.name: Pell’s Trailer
norcal_military_base.blurb: A field surgeon who left the Estero Bay COG under circumstances nobody explains, set up in a trailer outside the Main Gate. Military-grade work at civilian rates, provided you never ask about her last unit.

norcal_military_base.name: Gate Surplus
norcal_military_base.blurb: A tarp-roofed lot outside the wire where the base’s cast-offs end up: vests with last year’s issue numbers, boots, and crates of mixed ammunition that nobody has counted.

kabuki.name: Ganymede Street Market
kabuki.blurb: The street the map names, and the stalls along it. Busy at every hour the Tyger Claws allow it to be.

kabuki.name: The Ivory Needle
kabuki.blurb: Ink at the front, chrome at the back, and a Tyger Claw sitting where they can see both doors.

old_japantown.name: The Paper Lantern
old_japantown.blurb: A narrow bar in a converted shopfront between the container stacks and the hotel, open because the family heads say so. The Kimen-Gumi drink for free and nobody else asks why.

old_japantown.name: Nakamura’s Counter
old_japantown.blurb: Six stools, one pot and a broth that has reportedly never been allowed to go cold. The mushrooms come from Mrs. Suzuki’s, and nobody asks where she gets them.

heywood_industrial_zone.name: The Shift Change
heywood_industrial_zone.blurb: A canteen by day and a bar by night in a gutted loading bay. Couriers, dock crews and Zhirafa contractors who are not supposed to be here eat at the same long tables.

heywood_industrial_zone.name: The Second Shift
heywood_industrial_zone.blurb: A clinic that fixes dock crews and factory hands fast enough to make the next shift. The surgeon has strong views on workplace chrome and will share them whether or not you ask.

heywood_industrial_zone.name: The Tool Crib
heywood_industrial_zone.blurb: The tool crib by a loading gate, where the day shift draws kit and the night shift signs it back in. Anything not signed back in is for sale at a fair price.

downtown.name: The Ledger
downtown.blurb: A hotel-lobby bar with no hotel attached, built for the fixers and execs of the Chamber of Commerce. The drinks are overpriced on purpose; it keeps the room select.

downtown.name: The Quiet Room
downtown.blurb: A private surgical suite above a hotel-lobby bar, booked by the hour by fixers who cannot be seen at a hospital. The bill has a line item for discretion, and it is the largest one.

new_westbrook.name: The Studio Audience
new_westbrook.blurb: A bar across the road from the walls of Network 54’s fake city, where The Combat Zone plays on every screen and the regulars bet on who walks out.

south_night_city.name: The Chapel Steps
south_night_city.blurb: A collective of food carts cooking on scavenged burners on the steps of the Union Chapel Building. Cheap, loud, and protected by whoever paid last.

south_night_city.name: The Slammer Dock Door
south_night_city.blurb: A folding table in the loading dock behind the Slammer, where a cousin of the Kanzaki Family sells guns by the box. Scythe Security patrols the street out front and has never once turned its head.

little_europe.name: Sacred Heart Pharmacy
little_europe.blurb: A pharmacy that stopped selling aspirin years ago and kept the sign. Imelda Voss does eye and ear work in the back room and will tell you which saint to thank.

upper_marina.name: Ruggels Way Surplus
upper_marina.blurb: Marine surplus on the waterfront: flares, dry bags, rope and crates that fell off boats at convenient moments. Hollis Ruggels has a story about every one, and none of them match.

the_hot_zone.name: Dead Reckoning
the_hot_zone.blurb: A ripperdoc working out of a gutted skyscraper lobby, on a generator, with a cooler of spare parts and Maelstrom’s grudging protection. Fast and cheap, and nobody asks what the cooler held last week.

little_china.name: Auntie Mei’s
little_china.blurb: Herbs upstairs, chrome downstairs. Mei Zhao sells the tea, her son does the surgery, and the Gold Dragons take their cut from both.

little_china.name: Dragon’s Tooth Pawn
little_china.blurb: A pawn shop whose window holds watches and jade and whose back shelf holds whatever the Red Chrome Legion pledged against a bad week. Nothing is ever redeemed on time.

university_district.name: The Annex
university_district.blurb: A lecture hall nobody has booked in years, turned into a surgical theatre by a med-school dropout. NCU Campus Security calls it a student service and does not ask what it teaches.

university_district.name: The Co-Op
university_district.blurb: The engineering students’ own shopfront: soldering irons, ex-lab kit and the contents of a Biotechnica skip, sold by people who haggle like they are defending a thesis.

the_glen.name: Ardent & Pryce, Consultants
the_glen.blurb: A quiet practice on a high floor, patronised by executives with a dozen reasons to avoid the corporate clinic. Everything is billed as consultation, including the anaesthetic.

the_glen.name: Gentry & Blake
the_glen.blurb: A private security outfitter’s showroom: heavy catalogues, serious prices and a salesman who measures you twice and says nothing about why.

old_combat_zone.name: The Quartermaster
old_combat_zone.blurb: Edgerunners Inc’s own supply cage, open to anybody who has worked a job for Brick Coleman or can pass for it. Dot behind the grille grades customers on a scale that has nothing to do with money.

watson_development.name: Hachiman Arms
watson_development.blurb: A licensed gunsmith on Industrial St, receipted, regulated and politely suspicious. Mr. Hachiman files everything in triplicate, including your face.

watson_development.name: Picket Line Clinic
watson_development.blurb: A clinic that opened in the first week of the Watson strike and never closed. Lucius Rhyne’s organisers pay in favours, and the surgeon charges everyone else the same and tells the NCCS exactly where she stands.

charter_hill.name: Ascent Outfitters
charter_hill.blurb: A boutique selling armour-lined coats to people who want to look like they are climbing the ladder and survive the fall. The fitting room has a window onto the Exec Zone wall, which is the real sales pitch.

santo_domingo.name: Lupe’s Rig
santo_domingo.blurb: A nomad medtech’s converted camper at the end of Dam Road, parked where the road runs out of rules. Travelling families come to be mended and leave with a jar of something she calls honey.

pacifica_playground.name: Funhouse Mirror
pacifica_playground.blurb: Behind Playland’s costume shop, a ripperdoc rewires the park’s performers, who need to be tireless and tourist-proof. The mirror maze out front is a good way to find out if you were followed.

rancho_coronado.name: Doc Moss’s Greenhouse
rancho_coronado.blurb: A collapsed greenhouse the Dirty Hippies share with a surgeon who installs hobby-grade chrome among the tomato vines. Improvised, cheap and smelling inexplicably fresh.
